thesis: This episode argues that Amazon is an incredible innovator, potentially surpassing Netflix, while Google's top-down innovation approach is distinct from the bottom-up models of its peers. It highlights Netflix's successful business transition despite a specific pricing error that caused significant stock decline and member churn, noting that such mistakes are rare in the industry.

claims.claim: Amazon is described as an incredible company that has done amazing amounts of innovation, arguably more than Netflix.
claims.quote: So let's take Amazon. An incredible company, done amazing amounts of innovation, arguably more than Netflix. Okay? And they're not nearly as much as we are about freedom and no rules, but they're about the two pizza lunches and they're so willing to fail.

claims.claim: Netflix successfully transitioned its business from DVDs to streaming, but the company made a 'tragic mistake' with pricing that caused the stock to drop 75% and members to quit.
claims.quote: And we made one tragic, I made one tragic mistake in it, which is the pricing for the combined plan had been $10. And the separate plans, we said should be $8 for streaming, which is about Hulu's price, and about $8 for DVD. So it was effectively a 60% price increase.

claims.claim: The pricing mistake sent an email to 20 million American families announcing a price increase with no new features, resulting in the stock going down 75% and lots of members quitting.
claims.quote: So we sent an email, I sent an email, to 20 million American families. So 20% of American society, a one day, and the price is going up by 20% or 60%, and you get to use two services, two websites instead of what. So less convenience, radically higher price in the middle of a recession. And no new features. No new features. So it did not go well.

claims.claim: Despite the ugly landing, Netflix successfully transitioned its business, doing what Kodak, AOL, and Blockbuster never did.
claims.quote: We did the thing that Kodak never did. We did the thing that AOL never did. We did the thing that Blockbuster never did, which is we did transition our business successfully. But we did not stick the land. We landed ugly. Let's just say that.

claims.claim: Google's approach to innovation is described as very super courageous but top-down, unlike the bottom-up approach of Netflix and Amazon.
claims.quote: The thing that struck me about your book that was so different than Google's approach is Google's approach is Google's approach always seemed to me to be this very super courageous but top-down set of ideas. So we want to build an autonomous car. And we're going to put unlimited money for unlimited years into that.

claims.claim: Ten years ago Google was all about 20% time, but that is kind of like all gone now, and big innovations like Android and Google Drive are massive projects.
claims.quote: And Google's a fascinating one because, of course, 10 years ago, they were all about 20% time. Yes. And then that's kind of like all gone. And the question is, what did they learn? You know, it's pretty hard to do innovation on one day a week. And the big innovations they did are things like Android and Google Drive and Google Docs and massive projects.
